observed: The street and revolving entrances lead into a lobby with a long reception counter, an elevator bank and waiting traders.
Small marked dials sit above the elevator doors; a directory and several abstract objects or machines stand along the walls.
A busy trading floor remains visible beyond the lobby wall, so the entrance belongs to a working exchange.
The lobby's lighter surfaces separate it from the warm, crowded trading floor behind it.
corrections: Remove brass from revolving doors, trim and decorative machines; reserve it for bound readings such as elevator dials with engraved scales.
Build lobby pieces as contributed plots, without treating the generated corporate sculptures and planters as approved assets.
Restore emblem-plus-price-line content on visible trading monitors, which are largely blank in this image.
Use orthographic projection and the camera-dependent cutaway rather than copying the image's projection drift.
The reference's ground-level trading floor is compositional context; the product's lobby and stacked exchange floors still follow the building model.

Colour audit 13 October: replace the foreground stone floor with the required timber floor; rear trading-room timber is not evidence of a timber lobby. Remove decorative gold from the directory, doors, globe and ornaments, remove glow/reflections, and lift dark glass/steel where outlined.
